presentingComplaint: Sudden onset severe crushing central chest pain for 2 hours, radiating to the left arm and jaw, associated with sweating and breathlessness.
history: 58-year-old man, known hypertensive and type 2 diabetic on irregular medication, active smoker (20 pack-years), presents with acute onset severe retrosternal chest pain that began at rest 2 hours ago while watching television. Pain described as crushing/heavy, 9/10 severity, radiating to left arm and jaw, associated with profuse sweating, nausea, and one episode of vomiting. No prior history of similar chest pain or known coronary artery disease. No recent trauma, no fever, no cough. Denies illicit drug use. Family history of premature CAD (father had MI at age 55).
examination: Anxious, diaphoretic, in obvious distress from pain. No pallor or cyanosis. JVP not raised. Precordium: no heaves or thrills, S1 S2 normal, no S3/S4, no murmurs. Chest clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, non-tender. No peripheral edema. Peripheral pulses palpable and symmetric.
imaging: 12-lead ECG: ST-segment elevation >2mm in leads V2-V5 with reciprocal ST depression in II, III, aVF - anterior wall STEMI
Portable CXR: no cardiomegaly, no pulmonary edema, no widened mediastinum
Bedside echocardiogram: anterior and apical wall hypokinesia, LVEF ~40%, no pericardial effusion, no mechanical complication
citations: ESC Guidelines for Management of Acute Myocardial Infarction in STEMI 2023
contraindications: Fibrinolysis contraindicated if active internal bleeding, recent hemorrhagic stroke, recent major surgery/trauma, or severe uncontrolled hypertension
Caution with beta-blockers if signs of cardiogenic shock or acute heart failure present
Assess for dual antiplatelet bleeding risk prior to loading dose
edgeCases: If presentation delayed beyond 12 hours without ongoing ischemia, reperfusion strategy differs (primary PCI still preferred if feasible)
Right ventricular infarction should be excluded with right-sided ECG leads if inferior STEMI pattern present (not applicable here - anterior STEMI)
Diabetic patients may have atypical/silent presentations; this patient had classic anginal chest pain
Door-to-balloon time <90 minutes is the key quality metric if primary PCI capable center; door-to-needle <30 minutes if fibrinolysis chosen
expectedMaiK: Classic anterior STEMI with diagnostic ST elevation and rising troponin - flag as time-critical emergency requiring immediate reperfusion (primary PCI preferred, door-to-balloon <90 min) and dual antiplatelet + anticoagulation per ACC/AHA and ESC STEMI pathways.
expectedNextQuestions: Time of symptom onset to determine reperfusion window
Any contraindications to fibrinolysis or dual antiplatelet therapy

Signs of hemodynamic instability or mechanical complications
expectedInvestigations: Renal function, electrolytes, glucose, lipid profile
